title: A tuple reducer permanently breaks a thread on resume: BinaryOperatorAggregate.from_checkpoint restores the value as a list
version: editable checkout 11ee18599 (no release version stated; upstream main 7daa3ab49)
observed_behavior: With a state key Annotated[tuple[str, ...], operator.add] and an InMemorySaver checkpointer, the first invoke returns a tuple, but get_state() already shows a list; the next invoke on the same thread raises TypeError: can only concatenate list (not "tuple") to list, and the thread stays broken.
structure_focus: Reducer channel value type across a checkpoint boundary (checkpoint serialization + resume)
notes: Open, label external. Single-node graph plus checkpointer; issue body contains the exact minimal repro and traces the root cause to BinaryOperatorAggregate.from_checkpoint assigning the deserialized (list) value without reconciling it to the declared tuple type. The fixture represents the user-writable graph/state declaration; the defect itself is framework-internal and will only reproduce on affected versions (msgpack has no tuple type). Related set/frozenset report #8388 is explicitly separate.
